title: The Dead Return
question: What happens to the lanterns at the end of the festival?

meanings.usage: 指文化或宗教庆祝活动
通常指纸糊的照明灯具
the + 形容词，表示一类人
指从一个地方到另一个地方的路程
指引人注目的场景或表演
指聚集在一起的一群人
指海洋、湖泊或大河的岸边
指令人愉快的或受欢迎的
指运气不好或带来坏运气的
指令人感动或情绪激动的
指将物品整齐地摆放出来
指经过思考后形成某种看法
指认为某事会发生或应该发生

examples.en: He is said to be very rich.
examples.zh: 据说他非常富有。

examples.en: They are expected to arrive tomorrow.
examples.zh: 他们预计明天到达。

examples.en: Food was laid out on the table.
examples.zh: 食物摆在桌子上。

examples.en: The lanterns help the dead to find their way.
examples.zh: 灯笼帮助死者找到路。

examples.en: People dance and sing all night long.
examples.zh: 人们整晚唱歌跳舞。

examples.en: In the early morning, the food is thrown into the river.
examples.zh: 一大早，食物被扔进河里。

examples.en: It is considered unlucky to eat the food.
examples.zh: 吃那些食物被认为是不吉利的。

examples.en: Thousands of lanterns drift out to sea.
examples.zh: 成千上万的灯笼漂向大海。

examples.en: The lanterns slowly drift out to sea.
examples.zh: 灯笼缓缓漂向大海。

phrases.phrase: until they can be seen no more

examples.en: They watch until they can be seen no more.
examples.zh: 他们看着直到看不见为止。

sentences.en: A Festival for the Dead is held once a year in Japan.
sentences.zh: 日本每年举行一次亡灵节。

sentences.en: This festival is a cheerful occasion,
sentences.zh: 这个节日是个欢乐的时刻，

sentences.en: for on this day, the dead are said to return to their homes and they are welcomed by the living.
sentences.zh: 因为据说在这一天，逝者会回到他们的家园，受到生者的欢迎。

sentences.en: As they are expected to be hungry after their long journey, food is laid out for them.
sentences.zh: 由于他们长途跋涉后会感到饥饿，人们会为他们摆放食物。

sentences.en: Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way.
sentences.zh: 每家每户外面都挂着特制的灯笼，帮助逝者找到回家的路。

sentences.en: All night long, people dance and sing.
sentences.zh: 人们通宵达旦地载歌载舞。

sentences.en: In the early morning the food that had been laid out for the dead
sentences.zh: 清晨，为逝者摆放的食物

sentences.en: is thrown into a river or into the sea as it is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
sentences.zh: 被扔进河里或海里，因为活人吃了被认为是不吉利的。

sentences.en: In towns that are near the sea, the tiny lanterns which had been hung in the streets the night before,
sentences.zh: 在沿海城镇，头天晚上挂在街上的小灯笼，

sentences.en: are placed into the water when the festival is over.
sentences.zh: 节日结束后会被放入水中。

sentences.en: Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
sentences.zh: 数千盏灯笼缓缓地漂向大海，指引逝者返回另一个世界。

sentences.en: This is a moving spectacle, for crowds of people
sentences.zh: 这是一幅感人的景象，因为成群的人们

sentences.en: stand on the shore watching the lanterns drifting away until they can be seen no more.
sentences.zh: 站在岸边，看着灯笼渐渐远去，直到它们完全消失不见。

exercises.prompt: “用来说明动作发生时间的从句” 描述的是哪个语法点？
options: 陈述事实的过去时 (Simple Past for Facts)
宾语从句 (Object Clause) - I suggest that...
if 引导的条件状语从句
exercises.explain: 时间状语从句：when/after/before + 主语 + 动词...：用于描述两个动作的时间先后关系

exercises.prompt:
选出下面句子的正确中文意思：
are placed into the water when the festival is over.
options: 她敲击琴键太用力，结果两根琴弦断了。
我就用法语向他问好，他也用同样的语言回答我。
节日结束后会被放入水中。
exercises.explain: are placed into the water when the festival is over. — 节日结束后会被放入水中。

source.en: are placed into the water when the festival is over.

grammar.title: 一般过去时的被动语态
grammar.definition: 表示过去发生的动作，且主语是动作的承受者
grammar.structure: 主语 + was/were + 过去分词 + (by + 动作执行者)
grammar.usage: 当强调动作的承受者或不知道动作执行者时使用

examples.en: A Festival for the Dead is held once a year.
examples.zh: 亡魂节每年举行一次。

examples.en: The food was thrown into a river.
examples.zh: 食物被扔进河里。

examples.en: The tiny lanterns were placed into the water.
examples.zh: 小灯笼被放入水中。

grammar.title: be + 动词不定式（表示计划或安排）
grammar.definition: 表示按计划或安排将要发生的事
grammar.structure: 主语 + am/is/are + to + 动词原形
grammar.usage: 表示将来确定会发生的事或被安排的事

examples.en: The dead are said to return to their homes.
examples.zh: 据说死者会回到他们的家。

examples.en: The lanterns are to be placed into the water.
examples.zh: 灯笼要被放入水中。

grammar.title: 时间状语从句
grammar.definition: 用来说明动作发生时间的从句
grammar.usage: 用于描述两个动作的时间先后关系

examples.en: People dance and sing when the festival is held.
examples.zh: 节日举行时人们唱歌跳舞。

examples.en: The lanterns are placed into the water when the festival is over.
examples.zh: 节日结束时，灯笼被放入水中。

patterns.pattern: It is considered + adj. + (for someone) + to do something

original.en: It is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
original.zh: 对于任何活着的人来说，吃它被认为是不吉利的。

examples.en: It is considered impolite to ask about someone's age.
examples.zh: 询问别人的年龄被认为是不礼貌的。

examples.en: It is considered dangerous to swim alone.
examples.zh: 独自游泳被认为是有危险的。

original.en: Food is laid out for them.

examples.en: Books are placed on the desk.
examples.zh: 书被放在桌子上。

examples.en: The letter was sent yesterday.
examples.zh: 信昨天被寄出去了。

patterns.pattern: Thousands of + 复数名词 + 动词

original.en: Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea.
original.zh: 成千上万的灯笼缓缓漂向大海。

examples.en: Thousands of people gather at the square.
examples.zh: 成千上万的人聚集在广场上。

examples.en: Thousands of birds fly south in winter.
examples.zh: 成千上万的鸟在冬天飞向南方。

patterns.pattern: ...until + 主语 + can + be + 过去分词 + no more

original.en: ...until they can be seen no more.

examples.en: They watched the boat until it could be seen no more.
examples.zh: 他们看着那艘船直到看不见为止。

examples.en: She waited until the light could be seen no more.
examples.zh: 她等待着直到看不见那光。
